newsitem.title: ROMANIA: IMF REVISES ROMANIA 97 INFLATION ESTIMATE.
newsitem.headline: IMF REVISES ROMANIA 97 INFLATION ESTIMATE.

text.p: Romania's annual year-on-year 1997 inflation should be at least 130 percent, higher than earlier estimates for 90 percent, the IMF's chief negotiator for the country said on Thursday.
Poul Thomsen said the higher figure followed large price rises in February and March caused by price liberalisation.
But inflation for the second half of the year would be considerably lower, possibly below initial estimates under the centrist government's reform plans, he said.
Thomsen said initial figures showed July inflation between one and 1.5 percent, down from June's 2.3-percent rise and from a record 30.7 percent in March.

"These are only preliminary estimations. I understand it will be something like 1 to 1.5 percent (in July)," Thomsen said in an interview. "There is no doubt that it is below the programme assumption."
Thomsen, ending a month-long mission to assess the government's progress in introducing reforms, said the 130-percent figure assumed continued low figures for the second half of the year.
"(Inflation) will still be about two percent by the end of the year. Actually, I think it will be a bit below two percent."
Thomsen will issue a report on reforms to the IMF Board, which must decide whether to release the second of five $86 million loan tranches under a 13-month stand-by arrangement.
